contribution_requirements: AGENTS.md (root) mandates: before writing ANY Next.js code, read the relevant guide under node_modules/next/dist/docs/ for the APIs being touched, because Next 16 has breaking changes vs. training data. The single most important breaking change discovered: `middleware.ts`/`export function middleware` is DEPRECATED and renamed to `proxy.ts`/`export function proxy` (same signature: `(request: NextRequest, event: NextFetchEvent)`, same `export const config = { matcher }`). All role-based route protection (NextAuth v5 `auth(...)` wrapper, next-intl request handling) must live in `src/proxy.ts`, not `src/middleware.ts`. route.ts (Route Handlers) conventions are unchanged from recent Next versions (GET/POST/etc, `context.params` is a Promise). app/manifest.ts (or .json) for the PWA manifest is unchanged. Use npm, pin exact installed major versions, never invent APIs — when unsure about an installed library's App Router API (next-intl 4.14.9, @serwist/next 9.5.13, @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0), read its type declarations under node_modules/<pkg>/dist/*.d.ts or .d.mts first.
key_patterns: Reference-only OCR pattern from expense-tracker-ocr (do NOT import across repos, re-create locally): src/lib/cloudinary.ts exports `uploadImage(buffer, mimeType): Promise<string>` using `cloudinary.v2.uploader.upload` with a `data:` URI and a `folder` option, config read from CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME/API_KEY/API_SECRET env vars. OCR route (src/app/api/ocr/route.ts there) reads a `FormData` `image` field, uploads to Cloudinary (best-effort, swallows errors), then calls `openai.chat.completions.create` with model `gpt-4o-mini` (ledger-ocr should use a GPT-4o Vision-capable model, e.g. `gpt-4o`), a system prompt instructing JSON-only output, and a user message with a `type: 'image_url'` content part carrying a base64 `data:` URI with `detail: 'high'`; the JSON response is parsed with a markdown-fence strip + try/catch fallback. Both OCR and categorize routes in the reference project 503/500 cleanly when OPENAI_API_KEY is unset, checked via `if (!process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY)` before calling the SDK — ledger-ocr's ClassificationService/Vision service must do the same graceful-degradation check for OPENAI_API_KEY and TYPESAFE_API_KEY. next-auth v5 pattern (src/auth.ts there): `export const { handlers, auth, signIn, signOut } = NextAuth({ providers: [Credentials({...})], callbacks: { jwt, session }, session: { strategy: 'jwt' }, pages: { signIn: '/login' } })`; ledger-ocr's authorize() must bcryptjs.compare against the hashed password and must also carry `role` and client status onto the JWT/session (the reference app only carries id/email/name — insufficient for this task's role/status-based authorization, must be extended). The reference middleware.ts there is the OLD convention (`middleware.ts` + `export default auth((req) => ...)`); ledger-ocr must use the NEW `proxy.ts` convention (`export const proxy = auth((req) => ...)` or equivalent, matcher-scoped to /admin and /app) per node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/proxy.md. @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 real shape (node_modules/@typesafe-ai/sdk/dist/index.d.mts): `new TypeSafeClient({ apiKey })`, then `client.systemOne({ state, questions })` where `questions` is a map of named Question objects built with the exported `choice(instructions, criteria)`, `noul(instructions, criteria)`, `score(instructions, criteria)` helpers; the result's `answers[name]` is typed per question (ChoiceResponse has `.choice` + `.confidence` + `.probabilities`; NoulResponse has `.noul` as a 0-1 probability, no separate confidence field — treat `noul` itself, or `Math.max(noul, 1-noul)`, as the deductible confidence). Build ONE systemOne call with three questions: a `choice` for category (criteria = accountant's category names), a `choice` for btwRate (criteria = '0'|'9'|'21'), and a `noul` for isDeductible, as the task requires. next-intl 4.14.9 'without i18n routing' pattern (confirmed via node_modules/next-intl/dist/types and https://next-intl.dev/docs/getting-started/app-router/without-i18n-routing): create `src/i18n/request.ts` exporting `getRequestConfig(async ({requestLocale}) => ({locale, messages}))`, wrap next.config.ts with `next-intl/plugin`'s default export, read/set the active locale via a cookie (not a [locale] URL segment, since this app has role-based /admin and /app paths rather than localized routes) and wrap the root layout children in `NextIntlClientProvider` from `next-intl` (client re-export) for Client Components. Do NOT use next-intl/middleware's prefix-based routing (defineRouting + createMiddleware) since the task calls for cookie/profile-based locale selection (accountant defaults nl, client defaults es), not URL-prefixed locales. @serwist/next 9.5.13 pattern (confirmed via node_modules/@serwist/next/dist/*.d.mts and https://serwist.pages.dev/docs/next/getting-started): `import withSerwistInit from '@serwist/next'` default export wraps next.config; `swSrc: 'src/app/sw.ts'`, `swDest: 'public/sw.js'`; the service worker imports `defaultCache` from `@serwist/next/worker` and `Serwist` from `serwist`, declares `self.__SW_MANIFEST`, and calls `serwist.addEventListeners()`; app/manifest.ts (TS, not raw json) returns a `MetadataRoute.Manifest` object per node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/01-metadata/manifest.md.
